pr_title: kernel: system_work_q: Mark queue thread as essential
pr_body:
Fixes #70293 
Marking sysworkq as essential, so when it fails, the system will halt instead of continuously working, and dependent components stay in a broken state.
pr_comments: @andyross could you please share what can work as a better alternative to the `essential` feature ?

@ExtremeGTX an essential thread is just a watchdogging feature.  You're saying "this thread will never exit and if it does it's a fatal error and we should abort the system".  Better watchdogging is generally app-specific (e.g. "check in a k_timer ISR that events are still being processed" or "set a timeout at each event to make sure it's processed in time"), and ideally backed by watchdog hardware (e.g. "tickle the watchdog at each event or else it will autonomously reset the system").

Compared to that stuff "this thread died" isn't really that helpful, and I'd prefer to see it not pollute the kernel API, which doesn't really need to be the thing that provides watchdogging.

issue_context.title: Provide a way to mark System workqueue thread as K_ESSENTIAL
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
When system is highly dependent on system workqueue, (for example multiple drivers defer interrupt work to be done later by system workqueue) if the system workqueue thread crashed then a reboot is needed to get the system back up and running and there is no point in continuing to operate in such state.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The Best solution would be to make use of Zephyr `K_ESSENTIAL` flag. so when sysworkq thread crash the fault handler can act accordingly for all essential threads in the system without special `if` statements or trying to match thread name to do special handling.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
use `k_thread_foreach` to loop over all threads to find the sysworkq thread by its name then act.

**Additional context**
Add any other context or graphics (drag-and-drop an image) about the feature request here.
comments: @henrikbrixandersen Should I make it configurable via KCONFIG ?

> @henrikbrixandersen Should I make it configurable via KCONFIG ?

I don't see why the system work queue thread would not be essential. I am actually surprised it is not marked as such already. I'd go for a solution without a Kconfig unless others can come up with a good reason for making it configurable.

review_comments: Your suggestion of adding it to the config probably makes the most sense - I should have clarified earlier

instead of making `essential` a global config for all work queues, it makes more sense to have a 'system' config, indicating this is a system work queue, then based on this, you can set the essential flag on system work queues.
Isn't there only 1 system work queue? Essential might be the better term 🤷🏼‍♂️

> and later on:
 `k_thread_create(&queue->thread, ...., prio, cfg->system_wq ? K_ESSENTIAL : 0, K_FOREVER);`

That means `bool system_wq` will be added to `k_work_queue_config` type without creating the new type `k_**sys**_work_queue_config`, otherwise we will need to have 2 implementations of `k_work_queue_start()`

> Isn't there only 1 system work queue? Essential might be the better term 🤷🏼‍♂️

there is only one, and hence the suggestion by only reading the PR description and the related issue, however, there is another commit in this PR that is not mentioned in the PR description which allows essential to be set on any work queue. I was commenting based on the PR description.
